The type of cataract that is specific for diabetes:
explanation_verbatim: Snowflake cataract is specific to diabetes, resulting from sorbitol accumulation in the lens due to high glucose. It presents as small, white, snowflake-like opacities in the cortex of the lens.

stem: A 92-year-old female patient came to the clinic complaining of gradual progressive diminution of the vision in her left eye. On examination, the visual acuity was hand motion, and the red reflex was absent. There was no fundus view in the left eye. The pupillary reflexes were normal in both eyes. What is the most probable diagnosis?

A 92-year-old female patient came to the clinic complaining of gradual progressive diminution of the vision in her left eye. On examination, the visual acuity was hand motion, and the red reflex was absent. There was no fundus view in the left eye. The pupillary reflexes were normal in both eyes. What is the most probable diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: In a mature cataract, the lens becomes completely opaque, causing absent red reflex and no fundus view. Pupillary reflexes remain normal since the optic pathway is intact.

stem: The most common type of intraocular lens used now is:
The most common type of intraocular lens used now is:
explanation_verbatim: The posterior chamber intraocular lens is the most common type implanted today, placed behind the iris and in front of the posterior capsule.

stem: Phacolytic glaucoma may occur in:
Phacolytic glaucoma may occur in:
explanation_verbatim: Phacolytic glaucoma occurs when lens proteins leak from a hypermature cataract, causing secondary open-angle glaucoma due to inflammatory blockage of trabecular meshwork.

stem: The type of laser used to perform a posterior capsulotomy is:
The type of laser used to perform a posterior capsulotomy is:
explanation_verbatim: Posterior capsulotomy after cataract surgery is performed with Nd:YAG laser to restore visual clarity by removing the opacified posterior capsule.

stem: An elderly man reports that he no longer needs reading glasses for near vision, but his distance vision has deteriorated (-2D). What is this phenomenon called?
An elderly man reports that he no longer needs reading glasses for near vision, but his distance vision has deteriorated (-2D). What is this phenomenon called?
explanation_verbatim: In nuclear cataract, the increasing lens density increases refractive power, temporarily improving near vision (“second sight”). However, distance vision worsens due to myopic shift.

stem: A 70-year-old man complains of gradual, painless loss of vision. Ophthalmoscopy shows an absent red reflex. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 70-year-old man complains of gradual, painless loss of vision. Ophthalmoscopy shows an absent red reflex. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: A mature cataract causes complete lens opacity and absent red reflex, leading to painless vision loss. The pupil appears white or grayish.

stem: What is the treatment for diminished vision 2 years after cataract surgery?
What is the treatment for diminished vision 2 years after cataract surgery?
explanation_verbatim: After cataract surgery, posterior capsule opacification may cause vision loss. It is treated with Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy, which creates an opening in the cloudy capsule.

stem: Which of the following represents imprinting of the iris lens on the anterior capsule of the lens from the pupillary margin?
Which of the following represents imprinting of the iris lens on the anterior capsule of the lens from the pupillary margin?
explanation_verbatim:
Vossious ring refers to imprinting of iris pigment on the anterior capsule of the lens from the pupillary margin (in case of blunt eye trauma).
Hypopyon -> Pus in the AC (usually in neglected open wounds of the globe with secondary infection) [post-traumatic infectious endophthalmitis].
Hyphema -> Haemorrhage in the anterior chamber. The source of bleeding is the iris root.

stem: A 58-year-old male patient presents with complete lens opacification. What is the best tool used to visualize retina in that patient?
A 58-year-old male patient presents with complete lens opacification. What is the best tool used to visualize retina in that patient?
explanation_verbatim: In case of inability to visualize the retina, due to the presence of a dense cataract, B-scan ultrasonography of the eye can be helpful to exclude the presence of retinal detachment or vitreous haemorrhage.

stem: Which of the following causes jet black appearance of the pupillary aperture?
Which of the following causes jet black appearance of the pupillary aperture?
explanation_verbatim: Pupil is jet-black in the newly born and starts to acquire a greyish tinge as the person gets older due to the continuous addition of new lens fibers throughout life causing light scattering; a process known as senile sclerosis. It is to be noted that in the absence of the lens (surgically removed or posteriorly dislocated), the pupil regains its jet-black color.

stem: Which of the following is the innermost layer of the crystalline lens?
Which of the following is the innermost layer of the crystalline lens?
explanation_verbatim:
The lens is divided into regions depending on the age of the lens fibres. Those regions are arranged from within outwards into:
The embryonic nucleus.
The foetal nucleus.
The adult nucleus.
The outer cortex.

stem: A 66-year-old male patient complaining of recent progressive difficulty in seeing far objects (myopic shift). He reports that he used to see perfectly before. Which of the following might be the cause of that patient's condition?

A 66-year-old male patient complaining of recent progressive difficulty in seeing far objects (myopic shift). He reports that he used to see perfectly before. Which of the following might be the cause of that patient's condition?
explanation_verbatim: Second-sight phenomenon -> Regaining the ability to read and do near work without near correction in a previously presbyopic patient. It is due to increased refractive index of the lens nucleus (inducing myopia). It is seen in early cases of nuclear cataract.

76-year-old man has noted visual distortion over the past week. His concern increased when he discovered that the distortion was in the right eye only. Straight lines viewed through my left eye remained straight. Visual acuity testing revealed OD 6/24, OS 6/6.
What further tests will help determine the source of the patient's vision loss?
explanation_verbatim: The Amsler grid detects central visual distortion typical of macular diseases like AMD. It helps localize macular dysfunction.

60 years old diabetic patient for more than 20 years is developing a nuclear cataract in his both eyes, and his visual acuity has decreased to OD 6/18 and OS 6/24. His vision bothers him while he is driving because he cannot read street signs. He went to an optometrist for new glasses but was told he needed cataract surgery. He was referred for cataract surgery in 2 weeks with a surgeon who has not examined his eyes. The patient asks your advice.
What do you recommend to help this patient?
options: Proceed with the surgery to help prevent a car accident.
Advise him to defer cataract surgery for at least 6 month.
Refer the patient to ophthalmologist to determine the impact of cataract on decreased vision.
Assurance of the patient and advise him to follow up regularly
